**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unchecked session validation failures**

With this production default enabled, `validateRefreshSession()` returns `{checked:false, valid:false}` when `user_sessions` is missing or its validation query throws in production. `refreshToken()` only rejects `sessionRotation.checked && !sessionRotation.valid`, so an otherwise-valid refresh JWT can still mint a fresh access/refresh pair while the session store is unavailable, contrary to the fail-closed production contract. Treat unchecked failures as invalid when session enforcement is enabled, or reject on `!valid`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize refresh-token rotation**

When two protected API calls both get a 401 at the same time, they both enter this refresh path using the same stored refresh token. The backend rotates refresh tokens, so the first call can persist the new token while the second call is rejected and then `refreshTokens()` clears storage and dispatches session invalidation, logging out a valid user. Share one in-flight refresh promise before retrying authorized requests.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail closed when session persistence throws**

If the `user_sessions` insert throws instead of returning an error object (for example, a Supabase/PostgREST network failure), this catch still returns `checked: false`. `loginUser()` only rejects `checked && !persisted`, so production can issue a 24h access token and refresh token without recording a refresh session, even though this change makes production session enforcement mandatory. Return `checked: true` when enforcement is enabled, as the missing-table branch now does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
